parsed_response.reasoning: The diff shows office365calendar refreshAccessToken spreads `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` into o365AuthCredentials and persists via prisma.credential.update. parseRefreshTokenResponse (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set) parses against minimumTokenResponseSchema (only access_token required) and then does `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` — injecting a literal string that overwrites the real refresh token in the spread, which is then written to the DB. The user's actual Office365 refresh token is thereby destroyed, breaking future local refreshes. Mechanism fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: The spread ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) merges parseRefreshTokenResponse's sync-mode output — only {access_token} plus the injected literal refresh_token:'refresh_token' — into the office365 credential that is then written to the database. Enabling credential sharing on a deployment with Office365 calendars replaces each user's stored refresh token with the string 'refresh_token' on the first refresh, so the credential can never be refreshed locally again and the user must reconnect the app.
